provenance.question_selection: Four development questions cover the predefined roles: revised result, retention, instrumental explanation, selected-observation scope. No prediction-driven filtering or adversarial optimization of retrieval conditions.

page_numbering: One-based physical PDF pages; printed page labels may differ.

references.reference_answer: The revised main analysis reports delta t = TOF_c - TOF_nu = 6.5 ns, with statistical uncertainty +/-7.4 ns and systematic uncertainty +8.3/-8.0 ns. The result is compatible with propagation at the speed of light within the reported errors.

required_facts.required_fact: The revised main-analysis arrival-time difference is 6.5 ns.
acceptable_expressions: a central early-arrival estimate of 6.5 ns
upper systematic error 8.3 ns and lower 8.0 ns

required_facts.required_fact: The measurement is compatible with light speed within errors.
acceptable_expressions: no significant departure from light speed
compatible with zero arrival-time difference within uncertainties

scope_constraints: Use the revised main long-extraction analysis, not the original 60.7 ns result.
Do not substitute the revised alternative waveform estimate of 3.5 ns or the short-bunch TT/RPC estimates.
The positive central value is not evidence of a statistically established faster-than-light effect.
Statistical and systematic errors must be distinguished; they may not be silently combined into one error.
references.citation_scoring_notes: The later paper alone is sufficient. PDF page 33 explicitly states the result and compatibility. Pages 3 or 28 supply the quantitative result but do not alone state the compatibility conclusion as explicitly; evaluate individual cited claims rather than require every listed page.

evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The main estimate, both uncertainty components and compatibility with light speed are stated together.

evidence.locator: Abstract and Results; printed abstract p.1 and Results p.25
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The revised main arrival-time estimate and asymmetric systematic uncertainty are repeated.

references.reference_answer: Both versions give a BCT-to-OPERA geodetic baseline of 731278.0 +/-0.2 m, or 731.2780 +/-0.0002 km. That reported baseline is unchanged between the versions.

required_facts.required_fact: The BCT-to-OPERA geodetic baseline is 731278.0 m.
Both versions report the same baseline value.
acceptable_expressions: the same in v1 and v4

scope_constraints: This is the BCT-to-OPERA geodetic baseline, not the 730.085 km effective neutrino baseline used in the relative-velocity calculation.
Do not confuse it with the target-focal-point to detector component of 730534.61 m.
Unchanged source statements do not prove independent replication of the geodetic measurements.
references.citation_scoring_notes: One page in each version directly supports the comparison. Do not demand methodology pages 9/11 when the answer only states the value and retention. A single-version citation supports that version's value but does not by itself document cross-version equality.

evidence.locator: Section 4; final paragraph before Section 5; printed p.9

references.reference_answer: OPERA found an improperly connected optical-fibre cable in the timing path, which introduced an extra delay, and a frequency offset in the OPERA Master Clock oscillator, which distorted event timestamps during the acquisition cycle.

required_facts.required_fact: An improperly connected optical fibre affected the timing delay.
acceptable_expressions: incorrectly connected optical cable introducing extra delay
optical-fibre connection reduced received light and changed timing

required_facts.required_fact: The Master Clock oscillator frequency was offset from its specification and affected event timestamps.
acceptable_expressions: frequency offset in the Master Clock
oscillator calibration or frequency error that caused timing drift

scope_constraints: Identify two instrumental problems; a generic statement about measurement error is insufficient.
Do not present the geodetic baseline or neutrino physics as the identified cause of the earlier anomaly.
The question asks about the identified timing problems, not for a numerical decomposition of the entire change in the final estimate.
Do not assert that these two issues were the only methodological changes; event selection and analysis also changed.
references.citation_scoring_notes: The revised paper alone is sufficient. PDF page 18 explains the bad optical connection; page 20 explains the oscillator frequency offset and timestamp effect. Page 16 independently states the frequency offset. Page 19 may supplement the fibre explanation but is not mandatory.

evidence.bounded_paraphrase: An optical cable connection reduced received light and introduced an extra timing delay; restoring the connection restored the earlier delay measurement.

evidence.locator: Section 6 and Section 6.1; printed pp.13 and 17
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The Master Clock oscillator had a frequency offset of 0.124 ppm, producing a timestamp error that depended on position in the acquisition cycle.

references.reference_answer: No. The original analysis used 16111 selected events, while the revision used 15223. The revised selection discarded about 5% of preselected events whose earliest detector hit was isolated in time and position, because such hits could be noise and bias arrival times early. The nominal running years remained 2009-2011, but the selected sample changed.

required_facts.required_fact: The selected event sample changed; it was not an unchanged-sample correction.
The revision excluded events with isolated earliest hits that could be noise and bias early arrival timing.
acceptable_expressions: earliest hits separated in time and space from the event bulk were discarded
isolated early detector hits were rejected because of potential noise or early-time bias

numeric_acceptance.optional_fraction: about 5% of preselected events; do not require an exact fraction or derive one from the two published totals

scope_constraints: Same nominal 2009-2011 running years do not imply the same selected event sample.
Do not treat the added late-2011 short-bunch test as the revised main sample.
Do not claim a newer 2012 data collection replaced the original main sample.
Do not infer that all differences between the two counts are exclusively and exactly accounted for by a percentage computed from these totals.
references.citation_scoring_notes: The v1 selection discussion on PDF page 11 and v4 exclusion rule on page 13 together support a concise qualitative comparison. For count-rich answers, the original total is explicit on v1 page 8 and revised total on v4 page 13; v1 page 11 supplies original components. These paired sets are sufficient examples, not requirements to recite counts. A v4-only citation does not by itself establish the original selection rule.

evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The original main analysis has 16111 events, with 7586 internal and 8525 external interactions.

evidence.locator: Section 3 and Section 5; printed pp.6 and 10
evidence.bounded_paraphrase: The revised main sample has 15223 events. About 5% of preselected events with isolated earliest hits were excluded because of possible timing bias.
